articles.title: 500 Milliarden Dollar vernichtet: Google-Bilanz verursacht historischen Kurssturz
articles.preview: Google hat einen historischen Kurssturz erlebt, der rund 500 Milliarden Dollar an Marktwert vernichtet hat. Dies ist hauptsächlich auf Bedenken hinsichtlich der Rentabilität von KI-Investitionen und verfehlten Umsatz-Erwartungen zurück.

summary.t: Google hat im vergangenen Quartal die Erwartungen der Anleger verfehlt, was hauptsächlich auf die Umsatzerwartungen von Google Services zurückzuführen ist. Die Investitionen in Künstliche Intelligenz werden zunehmend als zu teuer kritisiert. Der Kursverlust von rund 500 Milliarden Dollar innerhalb eines Tages ist der größte seiner Art. Die Sorge besteht, dass die Kosten für den weltweiten KI-Ausbau die Erträge übersteigen könnten. Der Absturz um 13 Prozent belastete den US-Aktienmarkt, insbesondere die Nasdaq.

Die Google-Suche wächst zwar um 12 Prozent, aber das Wachstum ist im Vergleich zu früheren Quartalen geringer. KI verändert die Art und Weise, wie Nutzer nach Informationen suchen, da KI-gestützte Suchergebnisse oft direkte Antworten liefern und den Bedarf an traditionellen Links reduzieren. Google versucht, dieses neue Suchverhalten zu nutzen, indem es Werbung in KI-basierte Antworten integriert.

Konkurrenz durch Unternehmen wie OpenAI und Anthropic verstärkt die Bedenken hinsichtlich der Rentabilität von Google's KI-Investitionen. OpenAI hat bereits einen Werbeumsatz von einer Milliarde Dollar erzielt und expandiert weltweit. Analysten sehen weiterhin Unsicherheit hinsichtlich der Einführung von Werbung in Googles Gemini-Chatbot. Es wird erwartet, dass Alphabet bis zur ersten Hälfte des Jahres 2027 weiterhin mit Gegenwind konfrontiert sein wird, bis das Unternehmen das Vertrauen in die Grundlagen der Suche und die KI-Monetarisierung wiederhergestellt hat.

articles.title: Microsoft plans to raise $25 billion in debt as it pursues AI buildout
articles.preview: Microsoft is planning to borrow $25 billion through the issuance of bonds. This financing will primarily support the company’s significant investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

summary.t: Microsoft announced it will issue $25 billion in bonds. The company’s AAA credit rating allows it to access favorable financing terms. The bond offering is expected to close on November 4th.

articles.title: Schwarzer Tag für Alphabet : US-Anleger verlieren den KI-Optimismus
articles.preview: Alphabet hat einen deutlichen Kursverlust erlitten, was die US-Börsen insgesamt belastet. Die Bedenken hinsichtlich der Kosten des KI-Ausbaus haben zu einer Verunsicherung der Anleger geführt.

summary.t: Die Aktie von Alphabet, dem Mutterkonzern von Google, ist um fast 13 Prozent gefallen. Der Börsenwert schrumpfte um rund 460 Milliarden Dollar, was den größten Marktkapitalisierungsverlust eines einzelnen Unternehmens an einem Tag in der Geschichte darstellt.
Der Konzern war operativ in die roten Zahlen gerutscht. Die Werbeeinnahmen waren schwach und der Umsatz enttäuschte. Der Free Cash Flow verdoppelte sich nahezu.
Anleger machen sich Sorgen über die Rentabilität der massiven Investitionen in Künstliche Intelligenz.

articles.title: Alphabet earnings miss reflects first real sign that AI is taking a bite out of search
articles.preview: Alphabet’s latest earnings report revealed a significant miss, primarily driven by a slowdown in search revenue. Simultaneously, the company is investing heavily in AI, particularly through its Gemini model.

summary.t: Alphabet’s search and other segment revenue grew by 12% to approximately $63 billion, falling short of estimates. This represents a deceleration from the 19% growth seen in the first quarter. The company acknowledged that search query growth was the strongest in five years, but this wasn’t enough to offset the impact of increased competition from AI-powered bots. “Personalized bots” are now seen as a potential starting point for commerce.

Analysts believe AI is beginning to impact search revenue. Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster highlighted the potential of AI-powered services. The company is investing heavily in AI infrastructure and services, particularly through its Gemini model. Google’s Gemini-powered enterprise services are gaining traction with customers. AI is accelerating ad development and driving product launches.

Alphabet’s cloud business is experiencing strong growth, with revenue more than doubling to nearly $31 billion in the quarter. The cloud backlog reached approximately $560 billion, reflecting significant demand for AI infrastructure.

articles.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
articles.preview: OpenAI has released a new Model Spec. This document details five core values for developing more advanced AI.

articles.title: AI buildout hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts
articles.preview: Google and Microsoft have lowered their forecasts for capital expenditures related to artificial intelligence infrastructure. This shift suggests a potential slowdown in the rapid investment seen in recent quarters.

summary.t: Microsoft reduced its 2024 capex forecast to $170 billion, initially projected at $175 billion. Alphabet maintained its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion, both figures below previous expectations. These adjustments signal a potential cooling in the hyperscaler’s aggressive AI spending plans.

Significant delays in third-party graphics processing unit (GPU) availability from providers like CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN are impacting Microsoft’s plans. CFO Amy Hood indicated these delays won't resolve until the first half of 2027, adding to the challenges in building out AI infrastructure.

Neocloud companies like CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN experienced share declines following the announcements. These firms, reliant on outside capital, face difficulties securing investment-grade credit ratings amidst rising interest rates and concerns about debt. The firm Firmus, backed by Nvidia, recently withdrew its plans to go public.

articles.title: As AI becomes more fractured, one name stands out: AMD
articles.preview: The artificial intelligence sector is experiencing instability as several companies face difficulties. Amidst this turmoil, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is emerging as a standout investment based on specific criteria.

summary.t: Several AI-focused companies, including CoreWeave (-15.5%) and IREN (-20%), are struggling. Yields on CoreWeave's 2032 notes rose to 15%, and its default-swap spreads nearly doubled in October. This instability is impacting chipmakers, particularly due to spending related to CoreWeave and IREN.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) dropped 8.1% due to Meta's financing plans and a supply warning from Lam Research. Consensus forecasts EPS of $1.94 and revenue of $13.06 billion for Q3, representing nearly 62% and 41% year-over-year growth, respectively.

The author’s investment screen prioritizes companies with above-average revenue growth (5%+ annually), EPS growth (7%+), upgrades, a PEG ratio below 3, and ROE/ROIC of at least 12%. Currently, AMD is the only company meeting these stringent requirements.
AMD CEO Lisa Su stated plans to substantially increase supply in 2027 due to ongoing AI order demand.

articles.title: Alphabet drags on Nasdaq futures as the stock faces a record post-earnings loss
articles.preview: Alphabet's stock is experiencing a significant post-earnings decline, and Microsoft’s Azure growth is driving a positive trend. These developments are impacting Nasdaq futures sharply.

summary.t: Alphabet shares fell over 10% in premarket trading. The company’s earnings report marked the first double miss for both earnings per share (EPS) and revenue since Q4 2022. Concerns about AI chat and agents impacting Google Search volumes were a key factor.

Microsoft shares rose in premarket trading. Azure experienced a 48% growth, becoming the company’s largest business. Microsoft also predicted up to $97 billion in second-quarter revenue, exceeding forecasts.

articles.title: KI-Investitionen tragen nicht überall Früchte
articles.preview: Die Investitionen der Tech-Giganten in Künstliche Intelligenz zeigen gemischte Ergebnisse. Microsoft erzielt positive Ergebnisse, während Alphabet mit hohen Kosten und sinkenden Einnahmen zu kämpfen hat.

summary.t: Microsofts Geschäftszahlen übertrafen die Erwartungen. Der Free Cash Flow stieg auf 18,6 Milliarden Dollar, und das Wachstum der Cloud-Sparte Azure beschleunigte sich auf 48 Prozent. Finanzchefin Amy Hood bezeichnete das Quartal als erfolgreich. Die Investitionen blieben mit 45,2 Milliarden Dollar hinter den ursprünglichen Plänen zurück, was hauptsächlich auf Lieferverzögerungen zurückzuführen war.

Alphabet sah sich mit hohen Investitionen in die KI-Infrastruktur konfrontiert. Der Umsatz stieg zwar um 20 Prozent, der Free Cash Flow verdoppelte sich und der Konzernumsatz enttäuschte. Die Werbeeinnahmen schwächten die Ergebnisse.

Analyst Jesse Cohen wies auf eine Verschiebung im Geschäftsmodell von Microsoft hin. Die zunehmende Nutzung von digitalen Assistenten und nutzungsbasierte Abrechnungen verringern die Bedeutung von Lizenzeinnahmen. Microsoft reagiert mit günstigeren KI-Modellen.

articles.title: Quartalszahlen der Tech-Riesen: Zwei Seiten der KI-Medaille: Google zahlt, Microsoft kassiert
articles.preview: Zwei Tech-Riesen zeigen gegensätzliche Ergebnisse im KI-Boom. Google investiert stark, während Microsoft einen enormen Gewinn erzielt.

summary.t: Microsoft verzeichnete einen Free Cash Flow von 18,6 Milliarden Dollar, was die Erwartungen deutlich übertraf. Die Cloud-Sparte Azure wuchs um 48 Prozent, was Analysten positiv überraschte. Finanzchefin Amy Hood bezeichnete das Quartal als erfolgreich. Die Microsoft-Aktie stieg um 3,5 Prozent.

Alphabet erlebte einen deutlichen Kursverfall, der den Börsenwert um über 400 Milliarden Dollar reduzierte. Trotz einer Verdopplung des Umsatzes der Google Cloud, stieg der negative Free Cash Flow enorm. Schwächelnde Werbeeinnahmen trugen ebenfalls zu den Problemen bei.

Beide Unternehmen investieren weiterhin massiv in Rechenzentren, wobei Alphabet mit hohen Kosten zu kämpfen hat. Microsoft reduziert seine Investitionen um rund fünf Milliarden Dollar aufgrund von Lieferverzögerungen.

articles.title: KI-Boom gibt Rückenwind: Microsoft legt makellose Zahlen vor
articles.preview: Microsoft hat im letzten Quartal unerwartet hohe Umsätze und Gewinne erzielt. Die Aktie reagiert mit einem deutlichen Kursanstieg nachbörslich.

summary.t: Microsoft verzeichnete im vergangenen Quartal einen Umsatz von 92,3 Milliarden Dollar, was einer Steigerung von 19 Prozent entspricht. Besonders hervorzuheben ist das Wachstum der Cloud-Sparte Azure, die um 48 Prozent auf 33,17 Milliarden Dollar anstieg.
Der operative Gewinn stieg um rund 20 Prozent auf 45,9 Milliarden Dollar, während das Nettoergebnis auf 4,89 Dollar pro Aktie anstieg.

articles.title: Anthropic’s public benefit structure creates unusual risks for IPO investors
articles.preview: Anthropic is planning a highly anticipated IPO, aiming for a valuation of over $1.5 trillion. The company’s unique public benefit corporation structure introduces potential challenges for investors.

summary.t: Anthropic is pursuing an IPO as a public benefit corporation (PBC). Other examples of PBCs include Warby Parker and Patagonia. The company’s S-1 filing states its goal is to “responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.” Seven co-founders hold significant voting power through a single share.

Anthropic established a long-term benefit trust and a public benefit fund with 847 million shares. The co-founders, including Dario Amodei, control 50.1% of the voting power. The company believes this group is uniquely equipped to oversee its mission.

Legal experts suggest Anthropic’s PBC structure could create tension. The ambiguity of the term ‘balance’ in PBC law means directors must prioritize competing interests – profit versus public benefit – which could create legal difficulties. Lawrence Hamermesh, a Delaware corporate law attorney, stated that it’s “good luck” to successfully pursue a damages claim against directors in a PBC case.
Anthropic has restricted access to certain AI models due to safety concerns.

articles.title: OpenAI and ServiceNow expand partnership across enterprise workflows
articles.preview: OpenAI and ServiceNow are deepening their collaboration. This expansion will integrate OpenAI’s models and agents into ServiceNow’s platform, and vice versa.

articles.title: Tech scare trade hits Nasdaq futures while crypto reels from its biggest-ever hack
articles.preview: Tech stocks are plummeting, driven by disappointing earnings, and a massive cryptocurrency hack is sending shockwaves through the market. The Nasdaq futures are experiencing significant declines as a result of these events.

summary.t: Several major tech companies experienced substantial premarket losses. Intel shares fell over 25% due to weaker fourth-quarter guidance, reflecting concerns about the PC market. Amazon’s shares dropped by over 7%, and Reddit saw a decline of more than 20% following a warning about potential visitor drops. Alphabet shares remained flat after a 12% decline on Thursday.
Binance revealed a security incident impacting $6.3 billion in assets. The exchange froze $3 billion, $800 million, and $1.56 billion respectively, linked to the hack.

articles.title: Marktbericht: DAX steuert auf großes Wochenplus zu
articles.preview: Der DAX steuert auf ein großes Wochenplus zu. Trotz steigender Ölpreise und schlechter Unternehmenszahlen bleibt der deutsche Leitindex stabil.

summary.t: Der DAX rutschte im frühen Handel auf 25.990 Punkte zurück, blieb aber in Reichweite der 26.000er Marke. Nach einem Plus von 1,3 Prozent am Vortag liegt das Wochenplus aktuell bei rund drei Prozent.

Die Ölpreise stiegen aufgrund von geopolitischen Sorgen und militärischen Aktivitäten rund um die Straße von Hormus auf zeitweise ihren höchsten Stand seit April. Brent-Öl steuert auf ein Monatsplus von rund elf Prozent zu, WTI auf ein Anstieg von rund 14 Prozent.

Die Bilanzen von Intel und Amazon enttäuschten die Anleger. Der Gewinn von Intel brach um fast 20 Prozent ein, während Amazon aufgrund hoher Kosten für KI-Rechenzentren einen Umsatzwachstum von 13 Prozent nicht erreichte.
Experten erwarten einen Rücksetzer, wobei die 25.650 Punkte Marke als erste Unterstützung dient.

articles.title: Amazon falls 7%, Intel plunges 25% in premarket trading, as pressure mounts after earnings
articles.preview: Amazon and Intel experienced significant premarket losses following disappointing earnings reports. This downturn has impacted broader tech stocks and futures markets.

summary.t: Amazon shares fell by 7% in premarket trading. The company missed its third-quarter earnings targets and maintained its $220 billion capital expenditure forecast for 2026. Furthermore, Amazon reported negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter.
Intel shares plummeted by 25% in premarket trading.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Kursschock bei Intel
Der Börsen-Tag: Amazon enttäuscht den Markt
Intel stock plunges 21% as chipmaker blames PC slowdown for weak guidance
articles.preview: Intel’s stock has plummeted significantly following a weak earnings report. The company cited a slowdown in PC sales and a factory explosion as key factors contributing to the drop.

summary.t: Intel’s stock price fell by more than 21% after the company issued a disappointing forecast for the fourth quarter. This was largely due to continued weakness in the global PC market, which saw shipments decline by 4% in the second quarter. Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and earnings per share of 43 cents, but Intel now anticipates revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion with earnings of 25 cents per share.

Despite a 21% increase in overall revenue – reaching $13.7 billion – certain segments struggled. Client computing and physical AI group revenue decreased by 5% to $8.1 billion. However, data center and AI revenue jumped by 78% to $7.3 billion. The company’s foundry business continues to face challenges.

The company’s operations were impacted by an explosion at a fab in Israel, which occurred earlier this month. This incident resulted in approximately $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters and an extended shutdown of the plant.

articles.title: Reddit shares sink on weak sales guidance and plans login requirement test as Google search traffic shrinks
articles.preview: Reddit shares plummeted following weak sales forecasts and plans to require all users to create official accounts. This shift comes amid declining search traffic from Google due to AI developments.

summary.t: Reddit’s stock price fell over 15% after the company’s third-quarter earnings report. Despite beating revenue expectations, the company provided a weaker-than-anticipated fourth-quarter sales forecast. This negative outlook impacted investor confidence.

A significant drop in search referral traffic from Google, down ‘meaningfully’ in the third quarter, is a key factor. This decline is attributed to Google’s increased focus on AI overviews and related AI features. This shift is driving Reddit’s plans to require user logins.

Reddit plans to require all users to create official accounts to access the platform. This change is being tested initially outside the U.S. in the fourth quarter. The company is still determining the functionality for logged-out users.
Daily active uniques rose 12% to 130.3 million, but U.S.

articles.title: Sorge ums Weihnachtsgeschäft: KI-Kosten reißen Milliardenloch in Amazons Bilanz
articles.preview: Amazon kämpft mit enormen Kosten für den Ausbau seiner KI-Infrastruktur, was zu einem erheblichen Einbruch der Gewinne führt. Investoren reagieren mit großer Besorgnis und der Aktienkurs brach ein.

summary.t: Amazon meldete einen fast sechsfachen Barmittelabfluss von 42,4 Milliarden Dollar in den letzten drei Monaten. Dieser massive Cashflow-Verlust ist hauptsächlich auf die hohen Kosten für den Bau neuer KI-Rechenzentren zurückzuführen. Portfoliomanager Wagner bezeichnete die Entwicklung als besorgniserregend, da das operative Geschäft zwar profitabel ist, die Investitionen dies vollständig verschlingen.

Auch andere Technologiegiganten wie Google, Meta und Microsoft erhöhen ihre Investitionen in KI-Infrastruktur. Google plant bis zu 205 Milliarden Dollar, Meta zwischen 135 und 145 Milliarden Dollar und Microsoft 170 Milliarden Dollar, wobei Microsoft seine Prognose leicht reduziert hat.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says Wall Street is punishing the wrong tech stocks
articles.preview: Jim Cramer believes Wall Street is overreacting to disappointing company earnings. He argues investors should focus on individual company performance rather than broad industry trends.

summary.t: The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite all experienced declines on Thursday. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.4%, while the Dow and S&P 500 each fell 0.4%.

Fortinet’s weak earnings negatively impacted Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike shares. Cramer highlighted that these companies offer more comprehensive cybersecurity platforms than Fortinet, which is primarily hardware-focused.
ServiceNow’s earnings disappointment affected Workday and Salesforce.

articles.title: Amazon posts negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion, holds 2026 capex unchanged
articles.preview: Amazon reported a significant negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion in the third quarter, driven by increased AI investments. Despite this, the company maintains its planned capital expenditure of $220 billion for 2026.

summary.t: Amazon experienced a substantial negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion over the trailing twelve months, a dramatic 386% increase compared to the previous year. Previously, the company reported negative free cash flow of $7.6 billion in the prior quarter. This outflow is primarily attributed to increased spending on property and equipment linked to Amazon’s AI investments.

Despite the negative cash flow, Amazon is sticking with its planned capital expenditure of $220 billion for 2026. Capital expenditures reached $77.3 billion during the third quarter, a significant rise from $35.1 billion a year earlier, exceeding analysts' estimates of $58.7 billion.

Amazon’s cloud segment, AWS, demonstrated strong performance, with sales soaring 39% year over year to $45.98 billion, surpassing consensus forecasts. Executives anticipate revenue growth rates of ‘over 40%’ next year and in 2028, citing investment in functionality and infrastructure.

articles.title: Amazon AWS posts 39% revenue growth as cloud rivals also accelerate
articles.preview: Amazon’s cloud division, AWS, experienced a significant surge in revenue, exceeding expectations. This rapid growth is mirroring increased investment in artificial intelligence by major tech competitors.

summary.t: Amazon Web Services (AWS) reported revenue of $45.98 billion for the third quarter, representing a 39% increase year-over-year. This figure surpassed the consensus estimate of $45.29 billion among analysts. The growth rate was also higher than the 37% reported in the previous quarter.
Major cloud rivals, including Alphabet and Microsoft, are accelerating their growth.

articles.title: Samsung Electronics shares slid despite record profit in the third-quarter
articles.preview: Samsung Electronics experienced a significant stock drop despite reporting record profits. The company plans a substantial return of capital to shareholders over the next few years.

summary.t: Samsung Electronics reported a third-quarter operating profit of 106.5 trillion won, a 783.11% increase year-on-year and a 13.85% rise from the previous quarter. Revenue rose by 126.88% compared to the previous year, marking a fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue and profit. The company also announced a 30 trillion won dividend payout, or 4,601 won per share.
Samsung intends to return 55 to 75 trillion won to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks. This total shareholder return is scheduled to be finalized at a meeting in late January 2027.

articles.title: Microsoft stock jumps 4% as cloud growth drives earnings and revenue beat
articles.preview: Microsoft’s stock experienced a significant jump of 4% following a strong earnings report. The company’s growth is primarily driven by its expanding cloud infrastructure, particularly Azure.

summary.t: Microsoft’s Azure cloud business experienced a remarkable 48% growth in its infrastructure, now representing the company’s largest single business. Revenue increased by 19% year-over-year, reaching $33.17 billion for the quarter, surpassing analyst expectations of $32.32 billion. Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood anticipates continued strong growth, projecting 49% to 50% growth at constant currency for the next quarter.

Microsoft is significantly investing in its data center infrastructure, with capital expenditures rising by approximately 30% to $45.2 billion. The company plans to spend over $50 billion in fiscal second-quarter capital expenditures, exceeding StreetAccount’s consensus of $53.10 billion. A large portion of these investments, around 75%, are focused on short-lived assets like Intel chips and Nvidia GPUs.

Despite increased capital expenditures, Microsoft is maintaining positive free cash flow. The company is exploring debt markets and other funding options, and free cash flow declined 27% to $18.63 billion. Microsoft is aiming for over $50 billion in capital expenditures and finance leases through 2027.
Microsoft’s ‘Agents and Infra’ segment saw revenue increase by nearly 25% to $76.8 billion, driven by Azure and Microsoft 365.

articles.title: CoreWeave and other neocloud stocks drop after Microsoft capex comes in below expectations
articles.preview: Several neocloud stocks, including CoreWeave and Nebius, experienced a significant drop in extended trading. This decline is linked to Microsoft’s lower-than-expected capital expenditure figures and broader concerns within the neocloud sector.

summary.t: Microsoft reported capital expenditures of $45.2 billion, falling short of the $50.7 billion average analyst estimate. This difference, combined with a 48% jump in Azure revenue, highlighted timing issues between receiving infrastructure and payment, impacting investor sentiment.

Microsoft’s $20 billion deal with Nebius for compute through the 2030s, and its status as a top CoreWeave customer, are now facing uncertainty. The lower capex figures suggest a potential delay in infrastructure delivery for these partners.

articles.title: As Waymo expands overseas, it remains a niche cash-burning business
articles.preview: Waymo’s international expansion is underway, but the company continues to operate at a significant loss. Despite revenue growth, Waymo’s operations are heavily reliant on Alphabet’s investment and are currently a minor contributor to the parent company’s overall financial performance.

summary.t: Waymo generated $372 million in revenue during the third quarter, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. However, the Other Bets segment, which includes Waymo, experienced a substantial operating loss of $2.05 billion, a rise from $1.43 billion the previous year. This segment also encompasses Isomorphic’s drug design research.

Waymo now operates in 15 U.S. cities and recently launched services in San Antonio, San Diego, and Tampa. The company plans to expand into Canada, Germany, Singapore, and Spain, with a targeted rollout in Germany slated for 2027, marking its first entry into the European Union.

articles.title: Chip-Werte gefragt: Wall Street legt nach Fed-Zinspause zu
articles.preview: Die US-Notenbank Fed hat den Leitzins unverändert gelassen. An der Wall Street erwarten die Anleger nun eine Zinserhöhung im Dezember.

summary.t: Nach der unveränderten Leitzinsentscheidung der Fed schlossen die US-Börsen am Mittwoch im Plus. Der Dow-Jones Index erreichte 52.475 Punkte, der S&P 500 7744 Zähler und der Nasdaq 26.550 Punkte.
Die Finanzmärkte erwarten nun eine Zinserhöhung der Fed im Dezember. Die Wahrscheinlichkeit dafür wird auf 85,0 Prozent geschätzt. Bisher lag die Wahrscheinlichkeit bei 78,3 Prozent.

articles.title: Jim Cramer sees major implications from SK Hynix's home-run quarter
articles.preview: Jim Cramer believes SK Hynix's strong earnings demonstrate a path for AI stocks to rally despite market skepticism. The company's surge has positively impacted other chipmakers, signaling renewed investor interest.

summary.t: SK Hynix reported earnings that exceeded expectations by approximately 6%. The company’s New York-listed shares rose over 13% following the announcement. This performance boosted other chipmakers, including Micron, Arm, and AMD.

Several factors contributed to SK Hynix’s success, including its low valuation of four times 2027 earnings. The company also projected shipment growth in the mid-20% range for this quarter, up from 10% in the previous quarter.
SK Hynix indicated that its production was sold out through 2029, supported by long-term customer agreements.

articles.title: Chipotle shares rise 7% after CEO says same-store sales growth will continue
articles.preview: Chipotle’s stock jumped after the CEO expressed confidence in continued sales growth. Despite margin challenges, the company reported positive same-store sales figures driven by changing consumer behavior.

summary.t: Chipotle reported a net income of $339.9 million for the third quarter, down from $382.1 million in the prior year. The restaurant-level operating margin decreased from 24.5% to 23.3%. Excluding certain charges, earnings per share were 27 cents. Net sales increased by 9.6% to $3.29 billion, largely due to the opening of new restaurants.
Despite initial concerns about raw lettuce and a subsequent jalapeno recall, Chipotle experienced same-store sales growth for the third consecutive quarter.

articles.title: Oracle stock pops 11% as long-term revenue forecast and clarity on financing ease debt concerns
articles.preview: Oracle’s stock experienced a significant surge, rising 11% on Wednesday. This jump was driven by a revised long-term revenue forecast and a plan to manage debt concerns.

summary.t: Oracle announced a projected revenue of $225 billion for fiscal 2030, anticipating an average annual growth rate of 35%. This significantly exceeds the 8% growth predicted by analysts polled by LSEG.

The company plans to raise a maximum of $20 billion in funding over the next three years, equally split between equity and debt. Vendor financing, customer hardware, and prepayments are expected to reduce cash needs.
